name: Biography of a Planet: The Life Story of the Earth
description: From a ball of molten rock to a world of oceans, forests and cities: 4.5 billion years of impacts, ice, oxygen, drifting continents and extinctions.

checkpoints.name: A molten beginning
checkpoints.note: The Earth forms from dust and rock, is struck by a Mars-sized body that throws out the Moon, and is pounded by impacts while its surface cools enough for the first oceans.

checkpoints.name: Oxygen, ice and the first animals
checkpoints.note: Single cells rule the planet for billions of years. Microbes fill the air with oxygen, ice may cover the globe, and the first soft-bodied animals appear at the very end.

checkpoints.name: Seas, forests and one great continent
checkpoints.note: Animals explode into variety, fish and plants move onto land, coal forests grow, and the continents merge into Pangaea before the worst extinction in history empties the world.

checkpoints.name: Dinosaurs and a falling rock
checkpoints.note: Life recovers and dinosaurs take over. Pangaea splits and new oceans open, until an asteroid strikes Mexico and ends the age of the great reptiles.

checkpoints.name: Mammals, ice and people
checkpoints.note: Mountains such as the Himalayas rise, the climate cools into ice ages, and mammals spread. Humans arrive late and now change the planet, which some call a new age, the Anthropocene.
